findings.message: This is an instance fix for the round-3 finding. The proxy now has its own `proxyWired` flag, but `wireProxy` still fills the shared `globalThis.amaxDb` (`shared.amaxDb ??= createDb(...)`). This diff does not change the gate inside `getDb()` in apps/web/lib/server.ts; only the `wireRateLimits` line changed. Round 3 described that gate as `cache.amaxDb`. On k3s and the standalone image, the proxy and the app share one process, and the proxy runs first on every request. So the app's `getDb()` finds the cache already set and returns the Db without wiring its own bundle: `configureRuntime`, `setGrants`, `setPrivacySources`, `installAuthorizer`, `configureAi` and its rate limits are never called there. Fix: gate the app's wiring on a module-scoped flag in lib/server.ts, separate from the shared Db cache, or have `wireProxy` keep its Db in its own module scope and leave `globalThis.amaxDb` alone. The new 'proxy first, then the app' case would catch this if it ran, so confirm it runs with a database in CI and is not skipped by `hasDb`.
findings.scenario: k3s pod starts, and the first request is a page. The proxy runs `wireProxy()` and sets `globalThis.amaxDb`. The app's `getDb()` then sees the cache set and skips wiring, so every service in the app bundle runs with no runtime, grants or authorizer, and fails or denies.

findings.message: `wireProxy()` returns false when `AUDIT_HASH_KEY` is missing or no Db can be made, and the proxy ignores that return value. It goes on to call `takeRate` with the unconfigured default limits and no recorder. Nothing is logged and nothing fails, so 'could not wire' looks the same as 'wired'. Page 429s are then never recorded in `api.rate_limited`, and the `AMAX_RATE_*` limits are silently replaced by defaults. Fix: when `wireProxy()` returns false while `DATABASE_URL` is set, fail closed, or at least log or flag it as not wired. Do not limit with defaults and drop the counts.
findings.scenario: On Vercel the proxy function's env has `DATABASE_URL` but no `AUDIT_HASH_KEY`. Pages are limited at the defaults instead of `AMAX_RATE_PAGE_USER`, and the API and webhooks screen shows 0 limited page requests.

findings.message: `byName` is one all-or-nothing choice for every name-only row, across every rule. Round 3 asked for a way to confirm or reject specific named rows, and this does not give one. A request often has name-only rows in several tables (presales activity, task, risk), or several people with the same name in one table. 'include' erases or exports all of them, including a namesake's rows. 'exclude' keeps all of them, including the subject's own rows, and the request still completes. No read tool shows the approver the actual rows to 'check' before deciding; the inventory gives only counts. Fix: take the decision per rule, or better per row id. Only list rows the approver has seen through a read tool. Keep the request open until every review rule has a decision.
findings.scenario: pt.task holds 'Rowan Test' rows owned by the subject and one by another Rowan Test, and presales.risk has a namesake's row. With `byName: "include"`, the other person's task and risk rows are anonymised. With `byName: "exclude"`, the subject's own task row is kept, and the request reads completed/Erased.

findings.message: Every name-review test seeds a single table (pt.task) with a single name-only row. No case covers name-only rows spread across two rules, or a namesake's row with the same spelling next to the subject's. Those are the variants where the single `byName` switch goes wrong. Add table-driven cases with two review rules, and with two same-name rows that belong to different people.
findings.scenario: Two review rules plus include: the test suite stays green while a namesake's rows in the second table are erased.

findings.message: `apiPlatform` no longer de-duplicates events by name and relies on every caller passing them through `webhookEvents`. If a caller builds the list another way, for example by concatenating `webhookEvents` results per module (a hand-built second copy, as `scripts/seed-demo.ts` has done for privacy sources), it registers two `fanOut` handlers for one event. Each delivery then goes out twice, under the less strict of two masks. Either keep the merge inside `apiPlatform`, or make it accept manifests rather than a pre-built list.
findings.scenario: `apiPlatform([...webhookEvents([a]), ...webhookEvents([b])], engine)` where a and b both emit `x.y.z`: each event starts two `api.webhook-deliver` workflows.

findings.message: [design] The Item doc comment still says name-only rows are listed 'for a person to check and change in chat'. That doesn't match the new design, where the approver decides with byName when completing the request. Update the comment.
